Pathophysiology 
of the Endocrine System
As mentioned previously, endocrine disorders are the result of 
hyposecretion or hypersecretion of hormones, or of hypore-
sponsiveness of target organs.1, 2 Table 17.4 outlines the most
common causes of endocrine dysfunction.
Primary hyposecretion occurs when an endocrine organ re-
leases an inadequate amount of hormone to meet physiologi-
cal needs. Secondary hyposecretion occurs when secretion of 
a tropic hormone is inadequate to cause an endocrine organ
to secrete adequate amounts of a hormone. For instance, if 
the thyroid gland produces inadequate amounts of thyroid 
hormone, this would be considered primary hyposecretion,
